On Monday, June 24, 2013 1:33:32 PM UTC-4, Julien Cornebise wrote:
Hi all

The attached code crashes Stan by violating an assert in eigen indexing operator.

New to STAN, I'm trying to code a simple multilayer perceptron in STAN, and the compilation works like a charm.
At sampling time, all the print() I've put occur properly, then the program crashes. I do not see where I am messing up my indices.

The problem is this line:

target ~ normal(mean_y, sigma_y);

target is of length 100, while mean_y and sigma_y are of length 2

before mean_y
mean y =[7.19592:0,1.13588:0]
before sigma_y
sigma_y =[1292.3:0,3.04109:0]

And it crashes when it tries to evaluate the log-likelihood of y[3]. I'm not sure what you were intending to do, but if you were expecting R style recycling where those two values get replicated 50 times each, then Stan doesn't do that automatically. You would have to explicitly construct vectors of length 100 and fill them in with the appropriate values.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Crashing STAN violating assert() in eigen
parts:
On Monday, June 24, 2013 3:32:20 PM UTC-4, Julien Cornebise wrote:
What puzzles me is that the print('after target') went smoothly, even though the evaluation just before it was the one crashing. Any pointer (besides the generated C++ code) that I should look at to understand this intricacy ?

I don't really understand it myself. When something like that happens, an exception gets thrown which eventually percolates up to something that catches it and decides whether the pull the plug on the sampler, which may or may not flush any print statements that have been lined up depending on whether you are using an R terminal, R via some GUI, or command-line Stan. Combined with high levels of optimization that let the compiler re-order things, I don't think you get a guarantee as to what prints when.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Crashing STAN violating assert() in eigen
parts:
Can the compiler really re-order in such a way that an
assert() doesn't stop the program where it occurs? I know
unspecified-by-the-standard behavior can change, but I'd
think order of statements would be guaranteed.

assert() is, of course, not an exception. If we get an
exception, it'll percolate up right away. Nothing catches
it other than the sampler. Again, I'd expect the error to happen
right away and that behavior to be guaranteed.

Also, behavior here should depend on debug status in R.
In Stan 1.3.0, I believe it's still possible to get an assert
if you're using set_cppo("fast") [which is the default].

This should change in Stan 2.0, so that the only way you
can crash R is if you configure a third mode that turns off
our error checking and lets thing go through to Eigen's library.

We don't want anything crashing RStan in debug() mode. In fact,
for 2.0, I really don't want anything crashing RStan in any mode
unless we explicitly warn the user when they configure.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Crashing STAN violating assert() in eigen
parts:
On Monday, June 24, 2013 6:19:33 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Can the compiler really re-order in such a way that an
assert() doesn't stop the program where it occurs?  I know
unspecified-by-the-standard behavior can change, but I'd
think order of statements would be guaranteed.

My suspicion is that the compiler might feel free to move the print() statements around a little bit because it recognizes that those don't affect downstream computations. But I think the more likely thing is that it buffers up print() statements, hits an assert(), and the assert() prevents the print() statements from flushing, possibly depending on whether you are doing command-line Stan, plain R, RStudio, R GUIs, etc.

Ben
